ground_truth.unit: change in the probability of marrying a commoner per percentage point of synthetic probability
ground_truth.location: Table 2, Panel A (Baseline), column (1) Married a commoner, Treatment
ground_truth.context: Table 2 ("The Season's Interruption and Marriage Outcomes, Probit, and OLS Estimation"), Panel A, column (1).  Probit of an indicator for marrying a commoner (a husband classed as a commoner rather than a peer, a peer's son or a member of the gentry) on the treatment: a woman's synthetic probability (in percent) to marry during the interruption of the London Season (1861-1863), the sum of the percentages of women marrying at her ages in 1861, 1862 and 1863 in "normal times", computed from a benchmark cohort of peers' daughters born 1815-1830 (excluding those who married after 1861 or died before age 30).  Controls: indicators for dukes', marquesses' and earls' daughters and for English peerages, and birth order excluding heirs.  Baseline sample: all peers' daughters aged 15-35 in 1861 who ever married, excluding second marriages, women married to foreigners and royals.  The entry is the marginal effect of the treatment on the probability (the paper reads it as a percentage- point change in the probability per percentage point of synthetic probability).  Standard errors clustered by birth year.

i4r.notes: DP47 Table 2 col 1 (replicates paper Table 2 Panel A col 1) 0.005 (0.002), N 644.

i4r.notes: DP47 Table 2 col 2 (replicates Panel A col 2) -0.004 (0.002), N 644.

cell.label: claude-code
cell.notes: attempt-1 was exploratory: it printed variable labels and summaries of data/final-data.dta and no RESULT lines. The final script uses the prepared flags base_sample (644) and marital_rates_sample (765), syntheticT as the treatment, and these outcomes: cOut, mheir, fmissmatch (absolute difference), fmissmatch2 (husband minus wife), fdown, and never married (nthismarriage==0, which is identical to celibacy). Controls are pr4 (duke/marquess/earl daughter), hengpee (English peerage) and biorder (birth order excluding heirs). Panel B adds distlondon. Probit columns report the average marginal effect of syntheticT, with delta-method SEs from a vcovCL birth-year cluster. OLS columns use feols with SEs clustered by byear. All claimed coefficients and Ns match on the first scored run, and the clustered SEs also match Table 2. No claim comparison or repair was needed. The bootstrap-t p-values were not computed because they were not claimed. No runs hung.
